name: sustained-glitch
title: Sustained Glitch
description: A scene that breaks up in short, scheduled bursts: torn slices, jumped blocks, red/blue channel split, then clean again until the next burst a second or so later. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a stat and a bar chart; label, number and bars from variables), not over the host video. The bursts are seeded, so the same seed breaks up at the same frames every render.
useWhen: A tech or developer-facing scene should feel unstable for its whole run without the corruption settling into a constant texture.
You want a recurring accent rather than an effect that lives at one cut: something breaks up every second or so and the frame recovers.
avoidWhen: The tearing should happen only at the cut between two scenes: use glitch-cut.
Only a headline should break up: use rgb-glitch-text.
You want continuous analog wear rather than intermittent faults: use vhs-filter.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Intensity
variables.description: How hard a burst tears the picture.

variables.label: Frequency
variables.description: Bursts per second (one chance per slot, some slots stay clean).

variables.label: Slices
variables.description: Number of horizontal bands that can tear.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Tears and blocks are coarse; 0.75 matches 1 in the stills.
